evidence: Reviewed staged diff in MyAccessibilityService.kt: findAndClickCloseButton now scopes candidate search to the popup subtree (findPopupContainer ascends from the Aceptar node to the outermost inset ancestor containing an ID node), prefers an explicitly named close node (close/cerrar/dismiss/descartar), then selects within the top 40 percent band of the popup preferring clickable candidates and the rightmost position, logging full bounds, clickable rank, and view id for every candidate; attemptNonCvClose verifies after a 300 ms delay that the offer popup actually disappeared before setting lastClosedId (picapOfferStillVisible), retries otherwise; build.gradle.kts version bump to 0.3.42

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt findAndClickCloseButton popup scoping and selection stages
findings.claim: The v0.3.41 device log showed the geometric topmost rule selected an ImageView at top=558 right=440 from eight candidates spanning the whole app window, performAction returned true, and the popup stayed open; in app mode the window is the entire Picap screen so list images and avatars competed with the close button. The new selection runs in four stages (named close node, top-40-percent band of the popup subtree, full popup, whole window fallback) and prefers clickable then rightmost. Consequence: the click targets the popup header corner instead of arbitrary window imagery, but if the popup layout puts the X outside the computed band or the popup container heuristic fails, the fallback stages can still select a wrong image; the full per-candidate bounds log makes any miss diagnosable from one logcat run, and the post-click verification prevents a wrong click from being recorded as closed.
proof_refs: device logcat CLOSE candidatos list shows eight window-wide candidates and the chosen one at top=558 right=440 with click=true but popup remaining
findPopupContainer ascends from the Aceptar node stopping at full-screen layouts and picks the outermost inset ancestor containing an ID node

findings.claim: Previously lastClosedId was set on performAction=true alone, which blocked all further scheduling for that id while the popup was still open (observed as ya cerrada previamente on the next events). Now the coroutine waits 300 ms and re-reads the windows (picapOfferStillVisible requires both an ID node and an Aceptar node); only a vanished popup sets lastClosedId and returns CLOSED, while a surviving popup returns CLICK_FAILED so the retry loop runs again. A false CLOSED is possible if the offer window is momentarily unreadable at verification time, and a false CLICK_FAILED would re-click a successfully closed popup, which degrades to a no-op because the later pass finds no offer window.
proof_refs: attemptNonCvClose calls delay(300) then picapOfferStillVisible before assigning lastClosedId
device logcat showed lastClosedId set after a non-closing click, blocking retries with ya cerrada previamente

findings.claim: findFirstNodeMatching and findPopupContainer traverse with getChild and parent, returning nodes owned by the caller while recycling discarded descendants and chain members; the full-screen ancestor is recycled only as a fresh parent instance and never the caller-owned rootNode. The recycling discipline is easy to regress: recycling the returned popup container before the click, or recycling a node that candidates still reference, would invalidate nodes mid-use. The code order (collect, click, then recycle) keeps the window roots alive until attemptNonCvClose finishes, and a mistake would surface as an IllegalStateException in logcat rather than a silent wrong click.
